summary: International context and timeline for CBI: the WTO sugar ruling (2004-05), the 2006 EU sugar reform and the end of the ACP Sugar Protocol (effective 2009), the July 2005 closure of the St Kitts sugar industry and the 2006 creation of the CBI-funded SIDF; and 2009-2026 visa, AML and EU/US policy events. Numeric content: FAOSTAT sugar cane, sugar production and export series for St Kitts 1961-2007, IMF sugar debt/export figures, IMF 2015 cross-country CBI estimates, and the European Commission's 2023 and 2025 per-country Caribbean CBI application/rejection/passport data (as submitted by governments). Almost all sources are official and stored in raw/; country figures in EU reports are self-reported by the CBI states and partly inconsistent between reports.

events.title: Australia and Brazil challenge EU sugar export subsidies at the WTO
events.description: Australia and Brazil requested WTO consultations with the European Communities over export subsidies under the EC sugar regime (Council Regulation 1260/2001), opening disputes DS265 and DS266. St Kitts and Nevis was among the ACP sugar exporters that asked to join the consultations.
events.quote: On 27 September 2002, Australia and Brazil requested consultations with the European Communities concerning the export subsidies provided by the EC in the framework of its Common Organisation of the Market for the sugar sector.

events.title: Thailand joins the sugar challenge (DS283)
events.description: Thailand requested consultations on the same matter, completing the three complainants (Australia, Brazil, Thailand).
events.quote: On 14 March 2003, Thailand requested consultations with the European Communities on the same matter.

events.title: St Kitts and Nevis reserves third-party rights in the WTO sugar panel
events.description: St Kitts and Nevis, then a Sugar Protocol exporter to the EU, reserved third-party rights in the single panel established on 29 August 2003.
events.quote: On 8 September 2003, Australia, Brazil, St. Kitts and Nevis, Tanzania and Thailand reserved their third-party rights.

events.title: WTO panel finds EU sugar export subsidies exceed commitments
events.description: The panel found that EC sugar exports had exceeded its annual commitment levels since 1995, that exports of C sugar and ACP/India-equivalent sugar received export subsidies, and that the EC acted inconsistently with Articles 3.3 and 8 of the Agreement on Agriculture.
events.quote: the European Communities' exports of sugar had exceeded its annual commitment levels since 1995, and in particular since the marketing year 2000/2001.

events.title: WTO Appellate Body upholds ruling against EU sugar regime
events.description: The Appellate Body upheld the core findings: footnote 1 of the EC schedule (covering re-exports equivalent to ACP/India preferential imports) did not enlarge EC commitments, and cross-subsidisation of C sugar was a payment on export; the EC exceeded its export subsidy commitments.
events.quote: The Appellate Body upheld the Panel's finding that the European Communities violated Arts. 3.3 and 8 by exporting C sugar

events.title: WTO adopts sugar reports
events.description: The Dispute Settlement Body adopted the Appellate Body report and the panel report as modified.
events.quote: At its meeting of 19 May 2005, the DSB adopted the Appellate Body report and the Panel report, as modified by the Appellate Body report.

events.title: Arbitrator gives EU until 22 May 2006 to comply on sugar
events.description: Arbitration under DSU Article 21.3(c) set the reasonable period of time for implementation at 12 months and 3 days.
events.quote: the arbitrator determined that the reasonable period of time is 12 months and 3 days, expiring on 22 May 2006.

events.title: St Kitts closes its state sugar industry
events.description: The St Kitts Sugar Manufacturing Corporation (SSMC) stopped production, ending some 350 years of sugar on St Kitts. The OECS counted 1,406 SSMC employees in July 2005 and put released workers at about 12% of the labour force; the IMF says about 1,400 workers or 6% of the labour force.
events.quote: On 30 July 2005, the sugar industry in St. Kitts and Nevis was closed resulting in the release of over one thousand workers

events.title: Government takes on the sugar company's debt (29% of GDP)
events.description: According to the IMF, the closure required the government to service the SSMC debt, equal to 29% of GDP, via a 30-year bond mostly held by the state-majority National Bank and secured by about 4,700 acres of land; the industry had lost 3–4% of GDP a year.
events.quote: The closure has required the government to service the debt of the sugar company (29 percent of GDP).

events.title: SSMC debt folded into central government debt
events.description: IMF tables include the St Kitts Sugar Manufacturing Company debt in central government debt from 2006.
events.quote: 8/ St. Kitts Sugar Manufacturing Company (SSMC) debt included in central government debt since 2006.

events.title: EU adopts aid for Sugar Protocol countries hit by reform
events.description: Regulation (EC) No 266/2006 set up accompanying measures for the 18 Sugar Protocol countries (St Kitts and Nevis included), based on national multiannual adaptation strategies, with EUR 40 million for 2006. St Kitts prepared an "Adaptation Strategy in Response to the New EU Sugar Regime" (IMF CR 07/141, Box 2).
events.quote: establishing accompanying measures for Sugar Protocol countries affected by the reform of the EU sugar regime

events.title: EU sugar reform cuts reference prices
events.description: Council Regulation (EC) No 318/2006 replaced the intervention-price regime with reference prices falling from EUR 631.9/t (white sugar, 2006/07) to EUR 404.4/t from 2009/10, and cited the WTO panel and Appellate Body decisions on export subsidies.
events.quote: Following the recent decisions on export subsidies of the World Trade Organisation Panel and the Appellate Body on EU export subsidies for sugar

events.title: Sugar Industry Diversification Foundation created as a CBI route
events.description: The SIDF was established in 2006 as an independent foundation funded by CBI contributions to support diversification away from sugar; its income rose from under 1% of GDP in 2007 to an estimated 12% in 2013.
events.quote: the SIDF was established in 2006 as an independent foundation, funded by contributions from the ECP, to support the development and diversification of the economy away from the sugar industry

events.title: EU moves Antigua and St Kitts to the visa-free list (conditional)
events.description: Regulation 1932/2006 transferred Antigua and Barbuda, the Bahamas, Barbados, Mauritius, St Kitts and Nevis and the Seychelles to the visa-free list, applicable once bilateral visa waiver agreements enter into force.
events.quote: Antigua and Barbuda, the Bahamas, Barbados, Mauritius, Saint Kitts and Nevis, and the Seychelles should be transferred to Annex II to Regulation (EC) No 539/2001.

events.title: EU denounces the ACP Sugar Protocol
events.description: The Council denounced Protocol 3 on ACP sugar (guaranteed prices and quantities) for 20 ACP states including St Kitts and Nevis, with effect from 1 October 2009, noting the Community "will cease to guarantee prices".
events.quote: is hereby denounced on behalf of the Community with effect from 1 October 2009 with respect to [...] the Federation of Saint Kitts and Nevis

events.title: Visa-free Schengen access for Antigua and St Kitts begins
events.description: The EC signed visa waiver agreements with Antigua and Barbuda, the Bahamas, St Kitts and Nevis, Mauritius, Barbados and Seychelles, provisionally applied from signature — the first such agreements the Community concluded.
events.quote: the agreements are provisionally applied from the date of today's signature, 28 May 2009.

events.title: Sugar Protocol guarantees end
events.description: Date from which the Community's denunciation of the ACP Sugar Protocol took effect.
events.quote: with effect from 1 October 2009

events.title: European Parliament resolution on "EU citizenship for sale"
events.description: Parliament expressed concern that national schemes involving the outright sale of Union citizenship undermine the concept of Union citizenship (reported in the Commission's 2019 report; the resolution text itself was not retrieved).
events.quote: The European Parliament, in its Resolution of 16 January 2014, expressed concern that national schemes involving the "direct or indirect outright sale" of Union citizenship undermined the very concept of Union citizenship.

events.title: EU moves Dominica, Grenada, Saint Lucia and Vanuatu to the visa-free list (conditional)
events.description: Regulation 509/2014 transferred Dominica, Grenada, Saint Lucia, Vanuatu and others to Annex II, applicable from entry into force of visa waiver agreements.
events.quote: The imposition of the visa requirement on the nationals of Dominica, Grenada, [...] Saint Lucia, [...] and Vanuatu is no longer justified.

events.title: US FinCEN warns banks about St Kitts CBI passports
events.description: FinCEN advisory FIN-2014-A004 said illicit actors, including Iranian nationals designated by OFAC, were obtaining SKN passports through the CBI program, which it described as having lax controls. Routes then: US$400,000 real estate or US$250,000 SIDF contribution.
events.quote: certain foreign individuals are abusing the Citizenship-by-Investment program sponsored by the Federation of St. Kitts and Nevis (SKN) to obtain SKN passports for the purpose of engaging in illicit financial activity

events.title: Canada imposes visa requirement on St Kitts and Nevis
events.description: Canada cited concerns about passport issuance and identity management within the CBI program.
events.quote: Canada has implemented the visa requirement on St. Kitts and Nevis due to concerns about the issuance of passports and identity management practices within its Citizenship by Investment program.

events.title: IMF working paper on managing CBI inflows
events.description: IMF staff paper (Xu, El-Ashram, Gold) documented surging CBI inflows in St Kitts and Nevis and Dominica, warned of sudden-stop risk from visa-policy changes, and recommended sovereign wealth funds.
events.quote: The paper proposes a framework for managing inflows and savings from ECPs to contain macroeconomic risks, and it recommends the establishment of a sovereign wealth fund (SWF) where such revenues are large and persistent.

events.title: Vanuatu starts issuing large numbers of investor passports
events.description: The EU dates the significant increase in successful applicants under Vanuatu's investor citizenship schemes to 25 May 2015, three days before visa-free travel to the EU began.
events.quote: the suspension should apply to all ordinary passports issued as of 25 May 2015, date on which Vanuatu started issuing a substantial number of passports in exchange for investment.

events.title: EU visa waiver agreement with Dominica signed and applied
events.description: The EU–Dominica short-stay visa waiver agreement was signed in Brussels and applied provisionally from signature.
events.quote: Done at Brussels on the twenty-eighth day of May in the year two thousand and fifteen.

events.title: EU visa waiver agreement with Grenada signed and applied
events.description: The EU–Grenada short-stay visa waiver agreement was signed in Brussels and applied provisionally from signature.
events.quote: Done at Brussels on the twenty-eighth day of May in the year two thousand and fifteen.

events.title: EU visa waiver agreement with Saint Lucia signed and applied
events.description: The EU–Saint Lucia short-stay visa waiver agreement was signed in Brussels and applied provisionally from signature.
events.quote: Done at Brussels on the twenty-eighth day of May in the year two thousand and fifteen.

events.title: EU visa waiver agreement with Vanuatu signed and applied
events.description: The EU–Vanuatu agreement was signed and provisionally applied from 28 May 2015; it entered into force on 1 April 2017.
events.quote: The visa exemption has applied to nationals of Vanuatu since 28 May 2015

events.title: Canada imposes visa requirement on Antigua and Barbuda
events.description: Antigua and Barbuda citizens need a Canadian visitor visa from 27 June 2017; existing eTAs ceased to be valid. The document does not give Canada's reason.
events.quote: with effect from 5:30 am EDT on June 27, 2017, citizens of Antigua and Barbuda will need a visitor's visa/Temporary Resident Visa (TRV) to travel to Canada.

events.title: OECD lists CBI/RBI schemes posing high risk to the CRS
events.description: After analysing over 100 schemes, the OECD listed those potentially high-risk for the Common Reporting Standard, including the CBI programmes of Antigua and Barbuda, Cyprus, Dominica, Grenada, Malta, St Kitts and Nevis and Saint Lucia, plus Vanuatu's Development Support Programme. Criteria: personal tax under 10% on offshore financial assets and no physical presence of at least 90 days. The EC dates the OECD conclusions 16 October 2018; the list page says last updated 22 October 2018.
events.quote: The OECD has analysed over 100 CBI/RBI schemes, offered by CRS-committed jurisdictions, identifying the following schemes that potentially pose a high-risk to the integrity of CRS.

events.title: European Commission report on investor citizenship and residence schemes
events.description: COM(2019) 12 described the Bulgarian, Cypriot and Maltese investor citizenship schemes and investor residence schemes in 20 member states, and the risks for security, money laundering, tax evasion and corruption.
events.quote: Such schemes have raised concerns about certain inherent risks, in particular as regards security, money laundering, tax evasion and corruption.

events.title: Commission opens infringements against Cyprus and Malta
events.description: Letters of formal notice over investor citizenship schemes, arguing that granting nationality for pre-determined payments without a genuine link breaches Article 4(3) TEU.
events.quote: the European Commission is launching infringement procedures against Cyprus and Malta by issuing letters of formal notice regarding their investor citizenship schemes

events.title: EU partially suspends Vanuatu visa waiver
events.description: Council Decision 2022/366 suspended the agreement, from 4 May 2022, for ordinary passports issued from 25 May 2015, citing Vanuatu's investor citizenship schemes (over 10,500 passports by March 2021).
events.quote: is hereby suspended as from 4 May 2022 as regards citizens of Vanuatu holding an ordinary passport issued by Vanuatu as of 25 May 2015.

events.title: European Parliament calls for phase-out of CBI and pressure on Caribbean CBI states
events.description: Resolution with proposals to the Commission: CBI schemes "objectionable", should be phased out; asks the Commission to push visa-free third countries with CBI schemes — footnoted as Antigua and Barbuda, Dominica, Grenada, Saint Kitts and Nevis and Saint Lucia — to abolish them.
events.quote: Notes that a risk stems from third countries that have CBI schemes and that benefit from visa-free travel to the Union

events.title: Commission recommends immediate repeal of investor citizenship schemes
events.description: Recommendation C(2022) 2028: member states should repeal investor citizenship schemes and review golden passports and residence permits held by sanctioned Russian and Belarusian nationals.
events.quote: the Commission is urging Member States to immediately repeal any existing investor citizenship schemes

events.title: Caribbean CBI states suspend Russian and Belarusian applications
events.description: All five Eastern Caribbean CBI countries suspended examination of applications from Russian and Belarusian nationals (welcomed by the Commission).
events.quote: the Commission welcomed the decision of March 2022 taken by all five Caribbean countries to suspend the examination of applications from Russian and Belarusian nationals

events.title: Commission activates visa suspension mechanism for Vanuatu
events.description: Implementing Regulation 2022/693 suspended visa exemption for Vanuatu passports issued from 25 May 2015, 4 May 2022 – 3 February 2023: the first use of the mechanism on public-policy/security grounds (COM(2024) 366).
events.quote: It shall apply from 4 May 2022 to 3 February 2023.

events.title: EU suspends Vanuatu visa waiver in full
events.description: Council Decision 2022/2198 suspended the agreement for all Vanuatu nationals from 4 February 2023 after Vanuatu failed to remedy concerns.
events.quote: is suspended in whole as regards nationals of Vanuatu, as from 4 February 2023.

events.title: Visa exemption suspended for all Vanuatu nationals
events.description: Delegated Regulation 2023/222 suspended the visa exemption for all Vanuatu nationals from 4 February 2023 to 3 August 2024 (later extended to 3 February 2025 per Regulation 2025/11).
events.quote: The exemption from the visa requirement for all nationals of Vanuatu is suspended from 4 February 2023 to 3 August 2024

events.title: Six CBI principles agreed with the US Treasury
events.description: Caribbean heads of government agreed six principles with the US Treasury (denials, interviews, FIU checks, audits, passport retrieval, suspension of Russian/Belarusian applicants); first US-Caribbean roundtable in St Kitts.
events.quote: the Six CBI Principles agreed to by Caribbean Heads of Government in February 2023. [...] The first was held in St. Kitts and Nevis in February 2023

events.title: UK imposes visa requirement on Dominica over CBI abuse
events.description: UK visa regime effective 15:00 on 19 July 2023 for Dominica (and Honduras, Namibia, Timor-Leste, Vanuatu).
events.quote: Careful consideration of Dominica's and Vanuatu's operation of a citizenship by investment scheme has shown clear and evident abuse of the scheme, including the granting of citizenship to individuals known to pose a risk to the UK.

events.title: UK imposes visa requirement on Vanuatu over CBI abuse
events.description: Same UK measure as for Dominica, effective 15:00 on 19 July 2023.
events.quote: The changes to impose a visa regime on nationals of Dominica, Honduras, Namibia, Timor-Leste, and Vanuatu will come into effect at 1500 on 19 July 2023

events.title: EU monitoring report flags Eastern Caribbean CBI schemes
events.description: Sixth Visa Suspension Mechanism report: at least 88,000 passports issued by the five states, rejection rates 3–6%, costs as low as USD 100,000; Commission to convene joint committees under the visa waiver agreements.
events.quote: In certain cases, the cost per individual is as low as USD 100 000.

events.title: Four Caribbean CBI states sign MoA on US$200,000 minimum
events.description: Antigua and Barbuda, Dominica and Grenada signed on 20 March 2024 (St Kitts and Nevis dated its signature 19 March) a non-binding memorandum to raise and harmonise the minimum investment to US$200,000 by 30 June 2024, net of commissions, share applicant information, create a regional regulator by 30 June 2024 and ban "visa-free access" marketing.
events.quote: The Parties agree to increase and harmonize the minimum investment threshold of the CBIPs to an investment sum of two hundred thousand United States dollars (US$200,000), no later than 30 June 2024.

events.title: IMF urges regional CBI standards and minimum pricing
events.description: IMF ECCU staff report recommended common due diligence and disclosure standards and minimum pricing benchmarks to avoid a "race-to-the-bottom".
events.location: Policy recommendations, "Adopt common CBI program standards"
events.quote: minimum pricing benchmarks to avoid a revenue-erosive race-to-the-bottom competition

events.title: Commission reports Vanuatu has not remedied concerns
events.description: Commission report on the Vanuatu suspension; describes Vanuatu as the first and only country for which the suspension mechanism was activated.
events.quote: Vanuatu has been the first – and so far, only – country for which the visa suspension mechanism has been activated

events.title: Saint Lucia signs the CBI memorandum of agreement
events.description: Saint Lucia's Prime Minister Philip J. Pierre signed the MoA, making all five Eastern Caribbean CBI states parties.
events.quote: Party E. – Saint Lucia [...] Date: 3.06.24

events.title: US$200,000 minimum CBI price takes effect in five Caribbean states
events.description: OECS: minimum price for any CBI option US$200,000 from 1 July 2024; discounting declared illegal; interim 7-member regulatory commission planned.
events.quote: With effect from July 01, 2024 , all countries have agreed that the minimum price for any CBI options shall be US$200,000 .

events.title: EU moves Vanuatu to the visa-required list
events.description: Regulation (EU) 2025/11 transferred Vanuatu to Annex I (visa required); published 14 January 2025, in force on the twentieth day after publication. Vanuatu received 1,988 CBI applications in 2022-23 and rejected 27.
events.quote: in Part 1 of Annex I, the following entry is inserted after the entry 'Uzbekistan': 'Vanuatu'

events.title: EU Court rules Malta's golden passport scheme illegal
events.description: Grand Chamber judgment in C-181/23: Malta's transactional naturalisation scheme amounts to commercialising nationality and Union citizenship, breaching Article 20 TFEU and Article 4(3) TEU.
events.quote: which establishes a transactional naturalisation procedure in exchange for predetermined payments or investments and thus amounts to the commercialisation of the grant of the nationality of a Member State

events.title: Caribbean CBI states notify EU of regional regulator
events.description: The five countries jointly notified the Commission of legislation creating a regional regulator, reportedly including biometrics and a residency requirement for approved applicants.
events.quote: In August 2025, the five Caribbean countries jointly notified the Commission of the establishment of a regional regulator for the operation of investor citizenship schemes.

events.title: EU makes investor citizenship a ground for visa suspension
events.description: Regulation (EU) 2025/2441 (published 10 December 2025) added the operation of an investor citizenship scheme without genuine link as a ground to suspend visa-free travel for Annex II countries.
events.location: Article 1, new Article 8a(1)(e) of Regulation 2018/1806, PDF p. 6
events.quote: (e) the operation, by a third country listed in Annex II, of an investor citizenship scheme under which citizenship is granted to a person, in exchange for pre-determined payments or investments, without that person having any genuine link to that third country;

events.title: US partially restricts entry of Antigua and Barbuda nationals over CBI
events.description: Proclamation 10998 suspended entry as immigrants and on B, F, M and J visas, effective 1 January 2026.
events.quote: (i) Antigua and Barbuda has historically had CBI without residency.

events.title: US partially restricts entry of Dominica nationals over CBI
events.description: Proclamation 10998 suspended entry as immigrants and on B, F, M and J visas, effective 1 January 2026.
events.quote: (i) Dominica has historically had CBI without residency.

events.title: EU warns Caribbean CBI could trigger visa suspension
events.description: Eighth VSM report: about 107,000 passports issued by the five states; CBI is a potential ground for suspension under the revised mechanism; states should vet applicants "pending the discontinuation of those schemes".
events.quote: constitutes a potential ground for the suspension of visa-free travel under the revised Visa Suspension Mechanism.

events.title: FinCEN rescinds its 2014 St Kitts advisory
events.description: According to the St Kitts and Nevis Citizenship Unit, FinCEN formally removed advisory FIN-2014-A004 on 24 February 2026.
events.quote: The advisory, which had been in place since 2014, was formally removed on 24 February 2026
